headline: The Wall Street Journal reported that SpaceX was in talks to supply the Pentagon with AI computing capacity worth up to several billion dollars.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 2: the report is from 17 Jul 2026, not today, and is a second-hand relay of a Journal story.
importance_line: What changed: another large cloud supplier may serve US defence AI, which matters to the Pentagon and AI firms and, indirectly, to taxpayers, but the talks were only reported in July 2026, could collapse, and it is not known whether a deal followed.
summary: The Wall Street Journal reported, as relayed by Stocktwits on 17 Jul 2026, that SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket company that also runs the Grok AI business it gained by buying xAI, was negotiating to give the Pentagon data-centre computing capacity for AI at a cost of up to several billion dollars, and that people familiar with the matter said the talks could end without a deal. Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Oracle already supply the Pentagon with such capacity, so an agreement would add another large provider for AI work across the National Security Agency and military users.
notes: Link is the Stocktwits page where the Wall Street Journal report was read; the WSJ original was not read. Older news re-dated: Stocktwits page metadata says 17 Jul 2026 (Google News showed 11 Oct).
